summary: Revival round 4 of 5. Score 7.3 (round 1: 6.5, round 2: 6.8, round 3: 7.2 and cut; Caiman: 7; ship bar: 7.5). Every gate is green and I checked each against the JSON. The head is the big change. It is now a true sculpted volume (stored mesh 'Basilisk's crowned head', 77,884 triangles, closed, 0 crossings). It has a rolled snout with no vertical facet, a socketed slit-pupil eye, a nostril, an open gape, a hanging fang and a forked tongue, under a five-point crown. Face-on at 300 px it reads without the caption as a crowned serpent coiled round a green stone on an escutcheon. In hero-300 it now reads as a crowned reptile's head rather than a knot of bumps. The walls under the table carry domed scales instead of mirror polish. Those were round 3's main cut reasons, and both are largely fixed. It still does not reach 7.5, because most of round 3's secondary punch items were not attempted and the new work brings new faults. (1) The palm's ventral scutes are still ruled rectangular bars (palm.png), and the band past the morph is still flat planks with straight step edges (reverse.png). Item 4 is unchanged. (2) The hackles are still lanceolate fronds with a midrib. Their walls are terraced slabs with stair-stepped, combed ends (shoulder.png, reverse.png, side.png). Item 5 is unchanged. (3) The head reads more as a blunt rodent or gecko snout than a serpent's: a big bulging round eye and a smooth, scale-less skull dusted with pebbles. The crown points are still triangular plates with balls on stalks, and the right-hand point shows a flat decimation facet. (4) The sculpted neck meets the painted body in a scallop-shell fan that reads as a seam. (5) The pounced field has become clusters and double rows of dotted craters that read as braille and clutter the shield; their rims comb at grazing light. The wall scales also shear into stripes and checkers at the shield's corners. One more round can reach 7.5 on items 1-5 below. They are local, and none touches the gates beyond re-running them.
strengths: The head is a sculpted volume at last. In stones.png and hero.png the snout rolls into the skull with one continuous highlight, the eye is socketed with a slit pupil, the gape is open, and the fang hangs from the upper jaw. Round 3 item 1's vertical jaw facet and pillow-tile grid are gone.
The crown is scaled up as asked (fleurons 1.69-2.05 mm at the band, pearls 0.95 mm) and carries at 3/4. In face-300 it is about 45 px wide and reads as a crown over the head.
Face-300 names the subject without the caption: a crowned serpent coiled round a marquise tsavorite on a beaded escutcheon.
The walls under the table now carry domed round scales (side.png, hero.png, shoulder.png) in place of round 3's large mirror faces. The rim bead line is kept.
Fang land raised from 0.178 to 0.422 mm (round 3 item 7 met).
The coil laps the boss by 0.52 mm, and the dark crease under the stone is much reduced.
The shield's factory corners and the band stay crisp (bare-vs-finished.png), and the build is clean at three resolutions with 0 template patches.

checklist.item: One theme face to palm, nothing scattered
checklist.reason: The serpent-king runs from the crowned head and coil on the shield through hackles, wall scales and keeled scales to belly scutes. The pounced craters in the chief corners (face.png x 520-1120, y 480-620) are the only element that drifts toward scatter; see punch item 5.

checklist.item: Reads as its creature at 300 px without the caption
checklist.reason: face-300: a crowned serpent coiled round a green stone. hero-300: a crowned reptile head with an eye on the shield. The snout is still blunt enough to read as lizard or rodent before serpent; see punch item 3.

checklist.item: Figurative motifs have true outlines, no combing, smearing or stair-steps
checklist.reason: The hackle walls are stair-stepped and combed: shoulder.png x 600-1000, y 330-600; reverse.png x 350-1000, y 370-560; side.png x 280-450 and 1150-1330. The boss and coil outer wall streaks vertically at grazing light (shoulder.png x 1130-1260, y 380-560; side.png x 600-1000, y 290-350). The pounced crater rims show radial combing (head.png x 0-1000, y 200-600). The decimated crown has a flat facet on its right point (head.png x 1320-1430, y 270-480).

checklist.item: Stones sit in made settings and are visible
checklist.reason: The marquise tsavorite is flush in a 0.849 mm boss with a bright-cut bevel, fully visible face-on and at 3/4, with one stone in both the report and the preview.

checklist.item: No flat, blocky or mechanical CAD; forms are sculpted
checklist.reason: The head is now sculpted, but the palm scutes are ruled rectangular bars (palm.png x 400-1250, y 400-560; Belly-scutes artwork is straight bars with ruled grooves). The band past the morph is flat planks with straight step edges (reverse.png x 1150-1450, y 450-950). The hackles read as terraced slabs at 3/4 (shoulder.png).

checklist.item: Factory stock keeps its hard wall-to-face angles
checklist.reason: The escutcheon's cusped chief, point and wall-to-table edges stay crisp in bare-vs-finished.png, side.png and stones.png.

checklist.item: Silhouette distinct from Arachne, Manticora and the Reptilia tiles
checklist.reason: An upright escutcheon carrying a crowned 3D serpent head 4.5 mm proud, with a coil round a marquise. Nothing in the Reptilia sheet or the other Bestiarium rings shares it.

checklist.item: Large, medium and small forms; density and legibility at least Caiman's
checklist.reason: The table now beats Caiman: head and crown (large), coil, boss and hackles (medium), bordure, scales and pits (small). The palm and the band past the morph are still sparse ruled bars and planks, whereas Caiman and Ophidian carry true scale texture round the shank. The shoulders' hackles read as one ridged mass rather than layered plumage.

punch_list.zone: Layer 'Belly scutes' on the palm (theta 270 +/- 55) and the keeled-scale band past the morph (theta roughly 200-250 and 290-340, reverse.png's right-hand band)
punch_list.change: This was round 3's item 4 and it is untouched. Replace the straight ruled bars with shingled ventral scutes. Each plate is domed at least 0.12 mm, with a trailing edge curved by at least 0.4 mm of sagitta across the band, lapping the next by at least 0.15 mm. Drop the ruled groove lines. Blend the flat planks past the morph into keeled dorsal scales at 0.84 mm pitch over at least 3 mm, so that no straight transverse step edge remains.
punch_list.acceptance: palm.png (x 400-1250, y 400-560): curved, overlapping plates with no straight ruled line. reverse.png (x 1150-1450, y 450-950): scale texture, no flat plank or straight step edge. The Belly-scutes artwork shows curved, not straight, plate edges.

punch_list.zone: Layer 'Hackles into scales', 0-70 deg off the head, both shoulders (face.png flanks, shoulder.png, reverse.png)
punch_list.change: This was round 3's item 5 and it is untouched. Turn fronds into plumage. Taper each vane's width by 50% over its last third to a single point, curve each shaft by 8-12 deg, and shingle each row over the next by at least 30% of its length. Thin the midrib to 0.05 mm or remove it in favour of the graver barbs. Replace the cut vertical feather walls with a rolled edge of at least 0.15 mm radius, and remove the hard alpha truncations at atlas x of about 340 and 660 in the Hackles artwork, which make the terraced slab ends.
punch_list.acceptance: face.png (x 280-500 and x 1100-1320, y 480-920): pointed, curved, shingled feathers, not leaves with a midrib. shoulder.png (x 600-1000, y 330-600) and reverse.png (x 350-1000, y 370-560): no terraced slab ends, no stair-steps, no vertical combing on the feather walls.

punch_list.zone: Stored mesh 'Basilisk's crowned head': snout, eye, skull surface and the crown points
punch_list.change: Make the head a serpent's, not a gecko's. (a) Lengthen the snout by about 15% and flatten its top into a wedge with a defined canthus ridge from the nostril to the brow. (b) Shrink the eye ball by about 25%, set it under a brow shelf that overhangs it by 0.2 mm, and keep the slit. (c) Replace the pebble dusting on the skull with 5-9 domed head plates of unequal size (rostral, internasals, prefrontals, frontal, supraoculars, parietals), 0.08-0.12 mm proud, divided by V-grooves, plus small keeled scales on the temples that grade into the neck scales. (d) Give each crown point a fleur or trefoil outline whose ball sits on the leaf's tip with no stalk. (e) Re-decimate with feature or curvature preservation (or spend the template's remaining 124 kB) so no flat facet survives, then re-measure the sculpt land rows on the decimated mesh.
punch_list.acceptance: head.png (x 130-700, y 650-1150): a long, wedge-shaped snout with a canthus ridge, an eye under a brow shelf, and irregular head plates with no pebble field. head.png (x 400-1450, y 200-650): crown points read as fleurons with no ball on a stalk and no flat facet (x 1320-1430, y 270-480). hero-300.png: the head reads as a snake's head. Template still at or under 3,000,000 bytes with 0 patches.

punch_list.zone: The joint between the sculpted neck and the painted body (just behind the crown, over the boss's upper right); and the coil's outer wall where it laps the boss
punch_list.change: Remove the scallop-shell fan at the joint. Run the head mesh's neck at least 2 mm along the painted body and blend its scales into the body's 0.25-0.55 mm scales, matching the girth within 0.1 mm, so the hand-over has no ridge, ruff or change of scale. Fillet the coil's outer wall into the boss and field with a radius of at least 0.3 mm, so the wall does not streak at grazing light.
punch_list.acceptance: stones.png (x 1150-1300, y 560-740) and head.png (x 1350-1600, y 600-1000): one continuous scaled neck, no fan or ridge. shoulder.png (x 1130-1260, y 380-560) and side.png (x 600-1000, y 290-350): no vertical streaking on the coil or boss wall. face.png (x 600-1080, y 900-990): no dark line between coil and boss.

punch_list.zone: Layer 'Pounced field' (the 94 pits) and the bordure; layer 'Wall scales' at the shield's four corners
punch_list.change: Make the field a field. Either spread the pits as an even pounced ground at 0.5-0.6 mm pitch over the whole open field, or remove the clustered craters and double rows entirely. Either way, make it impossible to read a second dotted frame or the trefoil clusters in the chief corners. Close the bordure gaps on both lower flanks (Beaded-bordure artwork near atlas x 360 and x 640). On the walls, fix the sheared stripes and checkers at the corners (Wall-scales artwork x 150-330 and x 680-860) by laying the scales in true mm across the corner, or fading them into rim beads over 1.5 mm there.
punch_list.acceptance: face.png (x 520-1120, y 480-760): an even ground or a plain field inside one bead row, with no clusters or partial arcs. head.png (x 0-1000, y 200-600): no radial combing round the pits. shoulder.png (x 1000-1350, y 600-1000) and hero.png (x 300-560, y 700-950): round scales at the corners, no stretched stripes or checkerboard.
